obligations.finding: Complete packet interleaving and transfer coordinates preserve the represented finite map. Selected coefficients require injectivity on a declared class. The gcd alias witness is correctly restricted to one unit node with known nonzero amplitude.

The signal period is 2pi, Fourier coefficients carry 1/(2pi), jump differentiation carries 2pi i n, and recovered functions are equal almost everywhere with a separately declared right-continuous representative. Later integral L1 is unnormalized.

The inward coordinate at the right interval edge has the correct sign. The sine-integral limit and Gibbs constant agree with the figures. Exact native-edge synthesis removes that edge's Fourier truncation term; the smooth approximation remains.
Coefficient noise is explicitly a vector in the measured coefficient space. The complex least-squares functional and amplitude bound use the reciprocal selected-mask coefficient norm.

Residualization projects onto the actual background range. Positive rays are distinguished from signed lines; the complement has a negative profiled amplitude. The finite-gap theorem uses norm distance, not a squared objective without taking its square root. Binary-mask norm error agrees with the symmetric support partition.

The guide uses the kernel-secant condition, treats sparsity zero separately, and assigns separation zero to wide supports. The 2epsilon/gamma coefficient bound requires sparse truth and estimate; strict threshold 2epsilon/gamma recovers support under true magnitudes greater than 4epsilon/gamma. Model mismatch remains in the residual allowance and final edge error.

High moments begin above K. The two-edge hand example uses an odd high starting index and separates shifted moment coefficients from original jump amplitudes. The Hankel factorization uses a transpose, not an adjoint. The finite sample budgets are sufficient constructions, and the no-edge branch is a mathematical branch excluded from the inherited API.

The guide states a supplied-threshold guarantee with the matrix spectral norm and the square-Hankel entrywise factor q. It retains the exact true-three/native-two rank-ratio witness rather than claiming that the native largest-ratio heuristic satisfies the threshold theorem.

The coefficient inverse allowance, disjoint root disks with a strict Rouche boundary test, and Vandermonde singular-value allowance remain separate. Root disk radius is not silently treated as angular error; elementary power bounds require unit-node normalization. The conditions depend on true geometry and do not become noisy-data-only certificates.

Opposite jumps at separation delta make fixed finite measurements and Vandermonde conditioning collapse. Two translated thin pulses have small L1 function difference while their location sets remain far apart; the negative result concerns parameter or location-set stability, not a lower bound on their L1 function error.

The actual jump count L is separate from offset r. Indices (q0+q)N+r lie above K. In the illustrated Lmax=4,N=3,q0=2 design, nine base and four adjacent samples are disjoint and total thirteen; cubing preserves the four Gaussian nodes, whereas fourth powers collide them.

Adjacent cross-products carry the physical phase, with nonzero fitted correlation required. The chord error factor and half-separation branch margin are correct. Associated roots divide angular error by N, while large N narrows the branch margin. Asymptotic location rates require uniform local inverse bounds, a Hankel gap, nonvanishing coefficients, distinct aliases, and the stated branch margin. The offset residual is a fitted-model consistency test with its own nonzero denominator.

A unit-jump mean-zero sawtooth has norm T/4 and translation norm 2d(1-d/T). The inherited coefficient-one location bound fails for 0<d<T/2; the factor-two allowance is valid. The moved-endpoint counterexample and mean adjustment match Figure 18. The guide keeps L1 versus uniform error separate and does not claim a uniform L1 operator bound for raw Dirichlet sums.

Shared-node recovery requires rank of the actual stacked system. Confluent annihilation uses repeated factors; leading offset phase requires a nonzero leading coefficient. This is scoped as an algebraic extension, not a tested solver for arbitrary jets.

The rational 25-pixel dictionary has declared background and three masks, with uncovered pixels establishing rank. The larger raster is an illustration of the declared geometry. The seven-point star panel is a full-library least-squares residual outside that dictionary. The six-to-nine burst order failure and unusable zero per-method runtime entries remain visible.
